notes: Modern Israeli Hebrew, phonemic/broad. Every row is harvested from English Wiktionary via the kaikki.org machine-readable export (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Hebrew/kaikki.org-dictionary-Hebrew.jsonl, downloaded 2026-09-07, 17,744 entries); `sourceUrl` points at the Wiktionary page the row came from. PRONUNCIATION VARIETY: only pronunciations Wiktionary tags exactly `Modern-Israeli` are used. Biblical, Tiberian, Yemenite, Ashkenazi, Sephardi and Samaritan transcriptions were discarded (943 Biblical rows among others), as were the corresponding academic romanisations (kɛ́lɛḇ, yəḇīʾăḵā́) — those are consonantal/Tiberian and not learner-facing. TEXT vs VOCALIZED: `text` is the unpointed spelling exactly as Wiktionary lemmatises it, and is additionally required to equal the Academy's ktiv male (full) spelling reconstructed from the pointed form, so it is written the way a real user would type it. `vocalized` is the pointed headword, re-spaced to match `text` (Wiktionary head templates insert stray spaces such as הַ מִּזְרָח and use maqaf where the plain spelling has a space). VALIDATION: an entry is kept only when its Modern-Israeli IPA and its Modern romanisation agree segment-for-segment under a comparator that neutralises Wiktionary's own notation variation (shva na written ' vs spelled e, tsere written ei vs e, q for k, [ŋ]~[n], [ɛ]~[e], [r]~[ʁ]~[ʀ], [x]~[χ], and the variably-realised glottals of א/ע). This catches kaikki's mis-ordered `sounds` arrays, where a page's IPA for one homograph would otherwise be attached to another (ספר sipér paired with /saˈfar/, כפור kipúr with /ˈkfor/). 728 candidate entries were rejected this way; 12,494 more had no Modern-Israeli IPA at all. AMBIGUITY: unpointed Hebrew is genuinely ambiguous, and a row carries every reading Wiktionary attests for that spelling rather than a single one. `ipa`, `romanization`, `romanizationStressed` and `vocalized` describe the page's dominant reading (a real lemma, then the entry carrying the most senses, then part-of-speech order); `ipaAlternatives`, `romanizationAlternatives`, `romanizationStressedAlternatives` and `vocalizedAlternatives` hold the rest and are positionally aligned with each other, index for index. `vocalizedAlternatives` is present only where Wiktionary prints a distinct pointed form for each reading; where it prints one canonical form covering several pronunciations the field is omitted rather than have a pointed form asserted for a reading the source does not point (37 rows across the two files). 152 of 426 rows carry alternatives — 129 with two readings, 19 with three, 4 with four — and they are deliberately the core vocabulary a learner meets first: ספר (séfer / sapár / safár / sfár), ילד (yéled / yalád), בית (báyit / bét), בוקר (bóker 'morning' / bokér 'cowboy'), את (et / at), עם (im / am), שם (shem / sam / sham). Two readings count as distinct only when their segment sequence or their stress differs, so entries differing merely in notation are collapsed, while Hebrew's stress-only minimal pairs are kept apart. A reading is listed only where Wiktionary actually publishes a Modern-Israeli IPA for it. שלך is therefore still absent: its two possessive readings (shelkhá, shelákh) have romanisations but no IPA on the page, and a row offering only the 'osprey' reading would mark a correct engine wrong. For the same reason ספר does not list sipér — in modern full spelling that verb is סיפר, a different string. VOCALIZED SPELLING: Wiktionary titles Hebrew pages in ktiv male but points the headword defectively, so on two surfaces (בוקר, רועה) de-pointing `vocalized` yields the defective spelling rather than `text`; that is the source's own orthography, and `text` is always the full spelling a user actually types. A hand blocklist still drops vulgar entries. OPTIONAL SEGMENTS: Wiktionary parenthesises variably-realised segments. `ipa` resolves glottals out (/(ʔ)adaˈʃa/ -> adaˈʃa), the ordinary colloquial realisation, and keeps every other optional segment (/(h)u/ -> hu); both readings are listed in `ipaVariants`, and a scorer should accept any of them. NOTATION: normalised to one symbol per phoneme for internal consistency — resh is always ʁ (8 rows written r upstream), ɛ -> e (1 row), ŋ -> n (2 rows). Wiktionary's tie U+203F between two prosodic words was replaced with the space the text has. Divergences from Wikipedia's Help:IPA/Hebrew, kept rather than converted: Wiktionary writes the affricate with a tie bar (t͡s) where the help page writes ts, and transcribes phonemically (e, o) where the help page also lists the allophones [e̮], [ɛ], [ɔ]. Symbol inventory otherwise matches the help page. ROMANIZATION: `romanization` is Wiktionary's Modern romanisation with the stress acute stripped (shalóm -> shalom); `romanizationStressed` keeps the source string verbatim. The apostrophe in forms like k'ev rosh is Wiktionary's shva na, and in forms like shavua' its א/ע. SENTENCE TIER: 89 rows, the full attributable supply. Hebrew Wiktionary has 115 unpointed multi-word entries carrying Modern-Israeli IPA; 97 survive validation and the requirement that the IPA have one whitespace group per written word, and 8 more were hand-dropped as vulgar or obscure. That is the ceiling — it stops at 89 because Wiktionary simply has no more multi-word Hebrew entries with IPA, not because of a cutoff. Only 7 rows are full clauses (אני לא מדבר אנגלית, חבל על הזמן, ...); the rest are two- and three-word phrases and construct compounds, which still exercise cross-word vowel restoration but are shorter than a sentence. Wiktionary usage examples were not used: they carry pointed text and a romanisation but no IPA. SOURCES: rows come from the kaikki.org export except where that export lacks a field Wiktionary shows on the page; בוקר, בית and شكرا لك were taken from the Wiktionary pages themselves, fetched 2026-09-07 at the URL in each row's `sourceUrl`. NOT INCLUDED: nothing was synthesised, transliterated by rule, or inferred. Every reading is one Wiktionary publishes for that headword.
